one_liner: GPL C library of adaptive range coders, adaptive-CDF rANS and a BWT compressor that beats bzip2 on ratio everywhere and on speed on some files.
what_it_does: TurboRC is a C library (C++-compatible headers) of entropy coders: branchless 32/64-bit range coders driven by bit, nibble or byte predictors (simple, dual-speed, FSM), order-0/1/2 and sliding-context models, context mixing, RLE, gamma/Rice/variable-length integer coding, static and adaptive CDF range coding, and adaptive-CDF rANS with scalar, SSE and AVX2 dispatch. Every codec is a buffer-to-buffer call of the form size_t xxxenc(in, inlen, out) / xxxdec(in, outlen, out); the caller must store the original length. On top sits a BWT compressor (rcbwtenc/rcbwtdec: UTF-8 and LZP preprocessing, libsais suffix sorting, QLFC or context-mixing back ends) and a turborc CLI that benchmarks every codec and compresses files.
how_it_is_fast: The range coder is written branchless (renormalization and bit coding without data-dependent branches) and offers 8/16/32-bit renormalization output; adaptive models are simple shift-based probability counters. The rANS path updates an adaptive CDF and is compiled three times (scalar, SSE, AVX2) with a runtime dispatcher (anscdfini), plus 2-way interleaved static CDF coders. The BWT pipeline uses libsais for the suffix array, optional 16-bit BWT, LZP and UTF-8 preprocessing, and QLFC (quantized local frequency coding) feeding the range coder instead of MTF plus Huffman as in bzip2.
when_to_use: You need an adaptive (per-symbol updated) entropy coder, bitwise or multi-symbol, with context models or mixing, and want a fast tested implementation instead of writing your own range coder
Coding integer streams (gamma, Rice, large-integer VLC, zigzag delta) or 8/16/32-bit data where adaptive range coding beats static Huffman or tANS on ratio
A BWT compressor that outperforms bzip2 on ratio on every listed corpus and on speed on logs: NASA access log at level 20e8 gives 4.40% at 38.69/106.37 MB/s vs bzip2 5.8% at 15.71/83.16 MB/s
Adaptive-CDF rANS when decode speed matters more than encode: 'ans auto' on enwik8bwt decodes at 202.27 MB/s vs 88.54 MB/s for the order-0 range coder at about 1.5 points worse ratio
GPL-3.0 projects, or commercial projects willing to buy the offered commercial license
when_not_to_use: Static order-0 entropy coding at maximum throughput: README rANS/CDF rows are in the 100-630 MB/s range, while siblings hypersonic-rANS (about 3 GB/s enwik8 decode), FSE/Huff0 and pivco-huffman are an order of magnitude faster
Proprietary code without a commercial license: GPL-3.0 applies to the library as well as the CLI
When you need a documented stable container format or API reference: usage is 'see examples in turborc.c', raw codecs have no framing and the caller must keep the original length

Fast BWT decompression on general text: bzip2 decompresses faster than TurboRC 20e8 on enwik8 (43.39 vs 36.21 MB/s), Silesia (52.14 vs 34.69) and enwik9 (46.46 vs 37.90), and bsc 0e0 is slightly faster on enwik8 and Silesia at a slightly larger size
If you need independently reproduced numbers: no CPU, compiler or flags are given for the README tables and the '3x faster than the next fastest range coder' claim lives only on an external page

integration.dependencies: libsais (git submodule, clone with --recursive) for BWT; bundled libdivsufsort optional; pthread and libm on Linux
integration.min_toolchain: C; README lists GCC >= 4.6, Clang >= 3.2, Visual C++ 2022, MinGW-w64, Xcode >= 9
integration.platforms: x86-64 (default build uses -mavx -mpopcnt; make AVX2=1 adds -march=haswell), aarch64, RISC-V (rv64gcv), ppc64le, s390x, Apple M-series; 32 and 64-bit
integration.thread_safety: not documented; anscdfini() sets global function pointers for SIMD dispatch, so call it once before using codecs from several threads. rcbwtenc takes a thread-count argument, but the BWT path read in rcbwt.c calls libsais single-threaded
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the turborc CLI compresses files like bzip2 but uses its own format (no bzip2 compatibility); library codecs are a custom buffer API, not zlib/bzip2-compatible

gotchas: Output buffers must be at least inlen bytes; if the result equals inlen the input was incompressible and was copied verbatim, so the caller must record that and the original length
Default x86-64 make adds -mavx, so a default build will not run on pre-AVX CPUs; pick SIMD level at build time

Open issue #7 (Dec 2023, no maintainer reply) reports errors in the ans codecs on Linux ARMv8 with attached data; closed issue #2 was a level 25 decompression failure on enwik8 (2020); build failures on macOS were reported in #5 and #6 (closed)
include/anscdf.h uses cdf_t, which is defined in include/turborc.h, so include turborc.h first
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick TurboRC when you need adaptive or context-modelled coding (bitwise, order-1/2, mixing, integer VLC) or a ready BWT compressor; for static order-0 throughput, hypersonic-rANS, htscodecs, FSE/Huff0 or ryg_rans-style interleaved rANS are faster and more permissively licensed.
verified_claims_summary: The README's enwik8bwt table compares only TurboRC's own coders (for example 'ans auto' 116.76 MB/s encode and 202.27 MB/s decode at 24.85%; o0 range coder 88.20/88.54 MB/s at 23.33%); the 2026-10 BWT tables show TurboRC beating bzip2 on ratio everywhere and on both speeds on the NASA log (2.5x compress, 1.3x decompress, derived from page data), while trading wins with bsc. No CPU, compiler or flags are stated, and the '3x faster than the next fastest range coder' headline is backed only by an external sites.google.com page that is blocked here.
status_note: Actively maintained (README updated 1 Oct 2026, last commit 2026-10-02) by a single author since 2013; GPL-3.0 with a commercial license on request, built via make or Visual Studio projects.
